stemMd: A survey asked customers who renewed a subscription why they stayed. Most cited excellent service. The company concludes that poor service cannot explain why other customers cancelled. What is the flaw?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Service quality cannot influence subscription decisions.

options.label: B
options.textMd: A majority response never provides evidence.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The company should have asked only its employees.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Customers who renew cannot evaluate service.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The surveyed group excludes the customers whose reasons for leaving are at issue.

explanationMd: Selection on renewal leaves out cancellations. Satisfied remaining customers can coexist with dissatisfied former customers. Ask the departing group, or sample both groups, before drawing conclusions about reasons for cancellation.

distractorRationale.a: It can influence both retention and cancellation.
distractorRationale.c: Employees are not the relevant population either.
distractorRationale.d: They may evaluate it; they are simply the wrong population for the conclusion.
distractorRationale.b: Majorities can be informative in representative samples.
